subject: Re: Evaluation dataset exchange — gating, usage limits, and QA sprint
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@fathompay.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: FathomPay Legal <legal@fathompay.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation artifact handoff — first pass

Connor — thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a short, timeboxed evaluation: exchange a 30k-row transaction test set and a 50-case prompt pack so our fraud modelling team can sanity-check output quality. A few asks on our side:

- We need a clear usage covenant (no production re-use, retention limited to 60 days),
- A point of contact for redaction requests if we spot PII,
- A simple mutual action plan (MAP) with acceptance criteria and a go/no-go decision after the QA sprint.

I attached a manifest CSV with a sample index. Can you confirm Redwood's standard gating and any templated MPA you prefer?

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Product Manager, FathomPay
--- attachment: fathom-eval-sample-manifest.csv (text/csv, 8KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@fathompay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation artifact handoff — first pass

Sam — appreciate the clear asks. High level: we can accept the dataset under an ephemeral access agreement with the following constraints (short):

1) Use constraints: evaluation-only, no model training, no production inference on customer data.
2) Retention: artifacts stored encrypted in our sandbox for 60 days; customer may request immediate purge.
3) Auditability: we’ll provide access logs scoped to tokens and actions during the QA sprint.
4) PII handling: Redwood will apply the agreed redaction workflow; if you flag rows we’ll quarantine and notify within 24 hours.

Proposed next steps: I’ll circulate a one-page MAP that includes milestone dates for the QA sprint (kickoff, mid-run quality review, acceptance call). Karthik and Naomi — I’ve looped you for the technical and legal constraints.

Connor O'Brien
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--- attachment: redwood-mpa-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 24KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@fathompay.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation artifact handoff — first pass

Sam — quick technical clarifications from our side:

- Format: the manifest looks good; please include a column marking "sensitivity" (low/medium/high) per row so we can apply the correct redaction policy.
- Delivery: we will ingest via an S3 presigned upload to a controlled, ephemeral bucket; after ingest we’ll validate schema and checksum within 4 business hours.
- QA sprint: 10 business days of active evaluation where you get token-level logs and a shared quality dashboard.
- Acceptance criteria suggestion (proposal):
  * Precision >= 92% on the 10 critical fraud scenarios in the test set,
  * No critical PII leaks in a random 500-row check,
  * No more than 3 stability regressions compared to baseline responses.

Attached is a concise MAP with dates filled in for the sprint and the suggested acceptance gates. I called out a limited time window for model variants we will route to (standard/open quantized). If legal is comfortable we can sign this as an MPA and move the assets.

—Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@fathompay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: FathomPay Legal <legal@fathompay.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation artifact handoff — first pass

Thanks Karthik — the acceptance gates look reasonable. A few legal points flagged by our counsel:

- Need explicit non-derivative clause for the evaluation artifacts (no training, no derivative datasets),
- Clarify that logs provided are redacted by default and that we must sign-off before any full logs are handed over,
- Request for a 30-day notice before automatic purge if Redwood intends to keep a read-only backup for compliance (they prefer purge at day 60 with 30-day notice if retention extended).

We can provisionally agree to the MAP if those points are reflected in the one-page signature. Sam (Legal) is happy to do a short DocuSign on a final one-pager.

—Sam
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@fathompay.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation artifact handoff — gating, usage limits, and QA sprint

Sam — thanks for the clarity and the legal asks. We updated the one-page MPA to incorporate the non-derivative clause, explicit log redaction workflow, and the 30-day notice window for any retention extension. Highlights:

- Non-derivative clause: "Customer artifacts supplied under this agreement shall not be used to further train Redwood models or create derivative datasets; all use is limited to evaluation and debugging for the QA sprint."
- Logs: default redaction applied; full logs available only after joint review and explicit written consent from the named customer POC.
- Retention & purge: automatic purge at day 60; Redwood may request a retention extension with 30 days' notice — customer may deny such request.

If this matches what you need, we’ll send a DocuSign link for the one-page MPA and provision the S3 upload. Proposed timetable if signed within 48 hours:

- Day 0 (sign): S3 presigned URL + ingest window opens
- Days 1–2: ingest + validation
- Days 3–12: QA sprint (10 business days) with mid-sprint checkpoint on Day 6
- Day 13: acceptance call + decision (go/no-go)

Next actions: Sam (FathomPay) to confirm redaction column in the manifest and legal to confirm acceptance for DocuSign.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
